newsitem.title: UK: Mideast ULCC tanker rates slip for most routes.
newsitem.headline: Mideast ULCC tanker rates slip for most routes.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates for Mideast markets were weak on Friday amid signs of shrinking activity for large ships sailing east and west, shipping brokers said.
But much international activity was stifled by the Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S.
KPC fixed the 258,000 tonne Mariner for a Mideast/US Gulf, UK/Cont journey, at W45/W57.5.
"Mideast numbers have come off, one broker said. He saw the rate for Mideast/UKCont routes.
"The Eastern market is quieter. The Japanese have fixed all their December cargoes and the Koreans are not far behind."

West African rates for two-million-barrel vessels were steady to softer. Elf fixed the Iseult to the UK/Cont at W66 and brokers assessed rates for similar sized vessels travelling to the U.S. Gulf at W62.5.
Sun Oil fixed one-million-barrel ships for the same voyage and brokers saw this as the market level.

Markets for North Sea barrels moving transatlantic were deathly quiet. "There is no market," one German-based broker said. "We would be catching flies in the office but we cannot find any because they are all frozen over here."
Med markets were subdued. Rates for 130,000 tonners continue to fall with the Novorossiisk Suezmax terminal closed for maintenance until December 9, and good supply of tonnage.

But some brokers still felt that even taking these factors into consideration, Elf's fixture of the 136,000 tonne Donat at W80 from Sidi Kreir to the UK/Cont, with Med options, at least five points below the market.
Aframax owners were getting better rates for cross-Med voyages, though. Three 80,000 tonners were fixed at W110 and one 78,000 tonne ship went at W105. This was another slight rise.
